name: comp-266

frames.best_why: All five faders are in view with the 1k knob pulled up and ringed, showing the tracks at different heights.

tagline: Five thin faders stand in a row, each setting one audio band.
summary: A graphic equalizer: five vertical sliders spaced evenly under the heading Equalizer, each capped with a white pill handle and named by a frequency underneath.
appearance: The word Equalizer heads a row of five upright tracks. Each track has a white pill-shaped handle at a different height, with a bright white length beneath it, and a small grey frequency label sits under every track.
behaviour: Each handle slides up or down its own track between minus five and five and carries a soft ring while held; a small value tip is set to appear during use. The other four faders stay put.
demo_content: Five bands labelled 60, 250, 1k, 4k and 16K, opening at raised, slight boost, flat and cut positions.
search_phrases: five vertical sliders in a row
up and down bars for sound tuning
each slider sets one frequency band
use_when: A player or mixer needs a compact multi-band tone control with visible band names.
avoid_when: Bands, their defaults and the minus five to five range are fixed in the source with no props.
customise: Band labels, starting levels, the heading and the value range are all written in the source; adding a band means copying a block.
weight_why: Five small vertical sliders; nothing animates unless a handle is moved.

a11y.note: Each fader has a frequency name and arrow keys work, but the heading uses a legend outside any fieldset so the group is loose.

issues: No zero line or scale, so it is hard to tell a cut band from a boosted one.
The heading is a legend element with no surrounding fieldset.
polish_why: Even, quiet faders that read as an EQ, but with no scale marks for reference.
